voices.1: en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural (chosen voice), base rate -8%, directed per passage (render_edge.py)

tracks.room: Street level · Calle Imagen entrance (or the north entrance)
tracks.title: Welcome to the Setas de Sevilla
tracks.where: At street level on the Plaza de la Encarnación, by the Calle Imagen entrance, near the escalators and the ramp that leads down to level minus one; stand to one side, out of the flow of people. If you arrive by the north entrance, from Calle Regina and José Gestoso, play it there before you go down.
tracks.what: Metropol Parasol, known as las Setas, by Jürgen Mayer H. (J. MAYER H., Berlin), engineered by Arup, opened 27 March 2011. The four layers: the Antiquarium on level −1, the Mercado de la Encarnación at street level, the Plaza Mayor raised square, the walkways and the Mirador 360º on top. NEW in V5.1: on level −1 some ruins can be glimpsed through glass before entering the museum (andalucia.com; spot to confirm at O4). The route, the three lengths (V5.1 desk estimates, PLAN_V5_1 §Lengths: Full ≈ 70 min, Essential ≈ 40, Highlights ≈ 25; O17 pending), the Antiquarium's separate entry, access.
tracks.listen: What the Setas are, the four layers you will pass through from bottom to top to middle, and how the three lengths of this guide work.

tracks.title: Antiquarium — Found under a car park
tracks.where: On level minus one, at the entrance to the Antiquarium beside the taquilla, or on the first stretch of walkway inside, where the excavated remains first come into view.
tracks.what: The Antiquarium, the archaeological museum under the Setas, opened with the Setas in 2011; about 4,879 m² of excavated remains from the 1st century AD to the 13th century: Roman houses with mosaics, a Moorish (Almohad) house; remains of a 1st-century Roman fish-salting works also found on the site. NEW in V5.1: the dig history in one line (1991 traders' test dig, 1998 rescue excavation linked to the car-park plan, the big excavation 2003–2009, archaeology directed by Fernando Amores Carredano); the museum space by the architect Felipe Palomino González: a glass "membrane" around the ruins, transparent to translucent; one zone of direct daylight only; two lighting systems, for the architecture and for the remains. The look of the space.
tracks.listen: How a plan for an underground car park turned into Seville's most important surviving Roman site, and how its architect wrapped the ruins in glass and light.

tracks.title: Antiquarium — Seville stacked up
tracks.where: Inside the Antiquarium, on the walkway at the first good view down into the remains, ideally where you can see how deep they go.
tracks.what: The 1991–92 test dig on the site of the old Mercado de la Encarnación (Verdugo Santos, Larrey Hoyuelos and Murillo Díaz, commissioned by the market traders' cooperative): convent remains, an Almohad level about 3 m down, a late-1st-century Roman building about 7 m down, Roman deposits to about 9 m; groundwater and a shored pit; the Setas designed as "a structure that sits on the Roman ruins". V5.1: kept from V5 003; the opening now follows on from 002, which names the 1991 dig.
tracks.listen: How a small test pit paid for by the market traders showed that every age of Seville lay stacked under this square.

tracks.title: Antiquarium — Medusa, the guardian
tracks.where: Inside the Antiquarium, among the Roman houses, at the label for the Casa de la Columna, the House of the Column, with its Medusa mosaic.
tracks.what: Roman Hispalis under the Plaza de la Encarnación: houses with mosaics built and rebuilt in several phases from the mid-1st century AD. NEW in V5.1: 47 floors found, 33 with mosaics, about a dozen on show when the specialist study came out (López Monteagudo 2015, as reported by KRAMER; spoken in the past tense, audit 004.1), some in situ on the floor, some as vertical panels (KRAMER); the Casa de la Columna with its Medusa mosaic (VS-ANT), "laid out on the floor" (ACOM); KRAMER: "the warning and protective Medusa in a geometric composition", "depicted with an unhappy facial expression", at "the first stop, building D". Guardian line kept general (Romans put Medusa's head on floors as a guard), the specific one attributed to "her study" (López Monteagudo, via Kramer's review; one consistent attribution across 004–006, audit 004.2); no claim that she protects this house. In passing: Casa Romana, Casa de las Basas, Casa de la Noria (house attribution of the noria left open, audit row 25). Originals, replicas, photographs.
tracks.listen: Why this is Seville's best group of Roman mosaics, how much of it you can see, and why a Roman family put a Gorgon on the floor.

tracks.room: Level −1 · Antiquarium, walking through the Roman houses
tracks.title: Antiquarium — Bacchus and the dinner party
tracks.where: Inside the Antiquarium, heard while walking on through the Roman houses after the House of the Column. There is no fixed spot: play it as you go and read the labels. It names what to look for, never where it is.
tracks.what: POSITION-FREE WALK-ALONG (lead decision 30 Oct 2026, kept in V5.1). NEW in V5.1: the Casa de Baco, whose triclinium's main mosaic showed the triumph of Bacchus with Ariadne (KRAMER); the version with Ariadne in the carriage was "the most common motive in Baetica for a long time" (KRAMER; not claimed to be this floor, audit 005.1); drinking vessels at the corners of the mosaic floor of the Casa de Baco (ACOM; not tied to the triumph floor, audit 005.2); the Casa del Sigma and the sigma, the C-shaped curved dining couch (stibadium), label-dependent (TTS, general archaeological terminology); the Hospitium de los Delfines and its rare "unswept floor" (asarotos oikos) motif in a geometric composition, food scraps "remnants of a particular event" (KRAMER); marine fauna among the mosaics found, dolphins, fish and water birds (KRAMER; "found", not "on show", audit 005.6). Attributed throughout to "the study" (audit 004.2). Names only, as in V5: the Casa de la Ninfa, the Patio del Océano with a three-metre mural (VS-ANT; what it shows is not described). Check every name against the O4 label photos before release; whether each floor is on show is a label question.
tracks.listen: A Roman dinner party pieced together from the labels: the wine god's triumph, a curved couch, and a floor covered in leftovers.

tracks.title: Antiquarium — The two birds
tracks.where: Inside the Antiquarium, wherever you find a mosaic hung upright on a wall with two birds at its centre, the museum's emblem; if you haven't spotted it, play it as you walk on and keep looking. It never says where the mosaic is.
tracks.what: NEW TRACK in V5.1. The emblem: the "kissing birds" mosaic, the symbol of the Antiquarium, "at the centre of a large mosaic" and "reconstructed on the wall of the museum" (ACOM), "pieced together … displayed on the wall" (ACOM-B). Only these SEC facts are spoken as fact; neither source mentions a bowl. Lead decision 31 Oct 2026 (fact audit 006.1/006.2; replaces the HOLD): KRAMER describes, in the Hospitium de los Triclinia, "a perfectly executed geometric composition with two birds on a crater in a small square panel as the central motif", with two borders creating an illusory water movement and smaller zig-zag panels forming a wave effect. That this panel is the emblem is an inference (audit §2 #1), so it is spoken as a panel "that may be the same one", and its details only as what to look for "if the label matches". Dropped: "It began as part of a floor", "underfoot", "sharing a drink", "small" birds (all inferred). Why such scenes: KRAMER, mosaics alluding to the plants and animals of nature were common in Roman houses, especially in areas for passage; their meaning "always eludes us". No species, no century, no "kissing" as fact. Retitled from "Two birds and a wine bowl"; 005's cue updated.
tracks.listen: The mosaic of two birds that became the museum's emblem, a panel described by the study that may be the same one, and how Romans decorated their homes.

tracks.title: Antiquarium — The Almohad house
tracks.where: Inside the Antiquarium, at the label for the casa almohade, the Almohad house, the Moorish part of the excavation.
tracks.what: An Islamic house of the Almohad period, 12th–13th centuries, with traces of the surrounding Almohad neighbourhood; found about 3 m below the street in the 1991–92 test dig, against about 7 m for the Roman level. Context: the Almohad Great Mosque of Seville (ordered 1172) and its minaret, begun 1184, today's Giralda. NEW in V5.1: the Torre del Oro, ordered by the Almohad governor Abu l-'Ula, built in 617 AH (1220–21) (Ministerio de Defensa 2023); "it survived because it was buried" (audit §2, OPINION-safe), tied to the layers above it (convent, market; AAA91). The house is not named "Casa de la Noria" (audit row 25, unresolved).
tracks.listen: How a house from Almohad Seville sits a thousand years and only a few metres above the Roman city, in the age of the Giralda, and why it is still here.

tracks.title: Plaza de la Encarnación — A plaza with many lives
tracks.where: On level minus one, by the lifts that go up to the Mirador, beside the Antiquarium entrance. Play it while you wait; there is nothing you need to look at.
tracks.what: The Plaza de la Encarnación before the Setas: the Convento de la Encarnación (founded 1591), demolished under the Napoleonic decree of 1810; a wooden market by 1820; Melchor Cano's permanent market hall, built in the 1830s; the cut of 1948; demolition in 1973; the surface car park; the 1990s underground car-park plan that ran into Roman Seville. NEW in V5.1, both attributed to the operator (S-HIST): "more than 400 stalls of fresh products" and "the first known food market in the city of Seville" (audit #9); the 1973 reasons as the operator gives them: structural problems in the vegetable and fish stalls, the Tamarguillo flood, the first supermarkets (audit #8; supersedes the PLAN 007 NOT line by PLAN_V5_1).
tracks.listen: How one gap in the city, cleared by Napoleon's brother, was filled by a market, cars, archaeologists and finally the Setas.

tracks.title: Setas — Mushrooms of wood
tracks.where: Start it in the lift as the doors close; the second half plays as you step out onto the first stretch of walkway, among the timber of the parasols. Keep moving with the flow and stop at the rail only where you're out of the way.
tracks.what: Metropol Parasol by J. MAYER H. (Jürgen Mayer H., born 1965), winner of the 2004 international competition (65 entries). NEW in V5.1: two phases, ten projects in the second, winner made public on 12 June 2004; the brief: a public space for the city, compatible with the conservation and display ("puesta en valor") of the archaeological remains (IAPH-PH50, CL), so the ruins were in the brief from the start (corrects V4's "brief rewritten"); Mayer still in his thirties (SOLITUDE + IAPH-PH50); the fig trees named by the city (Cristo de Burgos), "centennial" per the operator (S-HIST says the ficus "in the Plaza de San Pedro", which adjoins it; age to confirm at O20 / city guide p. 114), listed by the City among Seville's "árboles singulares" (SEV-AS), spoken as "remarkable trees" (audit S21, 009.1); this is the fig-tree passage's only full telling (010 and 021 call back to it, audit M3); the timber named once as Kerto-Q. Kept from V5: engineered with Arup; Kerto laminated veneer lumber made in Finland, about 3,400 elements made at Aichach near Munich, 2–3 mm polyurethane coating; concrete trunks with the lifts; the "largest wooden structure" claim and what the engineers say. No visual reference before "By now you're out of the lift" (was "As you step out", route audit S1).
tracks.listen: How a two-round competition, a brief that already protected the ruins, a nickname nobody planned and thousands of pieces of Finnish wood made the Setas.

tracks.room: Walkway · south side (where the Giralda is in clear view)
tracks.title: Walkway — The Cathedral and the Giralda
tracks.where: Anywhere on the walkway, or at the Mirador, where the Giralda, the cathedral's tall tower, and the cathedral beside it are in clear view above the rooftops. Stop at the rail where you're out of the way.
tracks.what: The Giralda: minaret of the Almohad Great Mosque, begun 1184, the cathedral's bell tower since the conquest of 1248, about 97.5 m to the top of the weathervane. NEW in V5.1: the Giraldillo, the weathervane on top, a cast-bronze figure of Faith holding a banner (lábaro) and a palm, 1565–1568, 348 cm tall, symbolising the triumph of Christianity over Islam (IAPH-GIR); the name-origin story is NOT used (no official source found). Seville Cathedral: new church decided in 1401 (spoken "early in the 1400s" to keep to three dates); called by UNESCO the largest Gothic building in Europe; World Heritage with the Alcázar and the Archivo de Indias (the Alcázar is not claimed as visible). Link to the Setas: the cathedral's vaulting as a design cue is told in 009 and only called back here (hook, and the timber-vaults line; audit M3); MoMA's 1:200 model (2004–07) and its "cathedral without walls". The Almohads glossed as the Moorish rulers, with the Moorish remains under the square stated for every version (audit M2, lead decision 3).
tracks.listen: The tower and the church that gave the Setas one of its first ideas, seen across the rooftops, and the bronze figure of Faith that turns on top.

tracks.room: Walkway · west side (the Giralda on your left)
tracks.title: Walkway — The river, Triana and the Aljarafe
tracks.where: On the walkway, at a spot on the rail where the Giralda, the cathedral's tall tower, is on your left: you are then facing west, toward the river and Triana. Stand close to the rail so others can pass.
tracks.what: The view west toward the Guadalquivir; NEW in V5.1: toward the river, the rooftops of Triana on its far bank (STRIP, seville-tickets, SEC; PLAN_V5_1 views rule), with one general line on Triana, pottery as its main trade for centuries (JA-TRI, OFF; sailors dropped: UPO-TRI is a student article, SNIP, audit 011.1); beyond, the Aljarafe, the high ground west of the city (Triana itself is low riverside ground, not the high ground). Kept from V5: Roman Hispalis as a river port (D. González Acuña, "Hispalis, puerto romano de la Bética", 2010); the first-century fish-salting works excavated under the Plaza de la Encarnación (corridor paved with small bricks, five tanks, four of them excavated, filled on abandonment with rubbish, mostly compacted fish remains, out of use c. 70–120 AD). Not on view from here. Flamenco is not said (not in the source read).
tracks.listen: Why the river made Roman Seville a port, the potters' quarter across it, and the Roman fish-salting tanks found under this square.

tracks.title: Walkway — The glue that had to be baked
tracks.where: Anywhere on the walkway on the way to the steps up to the Mirador, walking slowly or stopped at the rail out of the way of others, with the timber panels of the parasols around you.
tracks.what: The timber structure of the Setas: Kerto laminated veneer lumber panels by Finnforest, engineered by Arup (the firm of the Sydney Opera House and Beijing's Bird's Nest stadium); more than 3,000 joints with glued-in steel bars, about 35,000 holes drilled; the joints glued with epoxy resin, tempered for heat, while polyurethane is only the 2–3 mm coating; the Fraunhofer WKI heat study; the 2007 redesign; the largest panel 16.5 m tall. ONSITE: O10 (joints and coating visible from the walkway).
tracks.listen: How thousands of glued joints were made to survive the Seville sun, and why the structure had to be re-engineered.

tracks.title: Mirador 360º — The highest point
tracks.where: At the top of the steps, on the Mirador 360º, the highest platform of the Setas. Find a place at the rail where you are not blocking the steps.
tracks.what: The Mirador 360º, the highest point of Metropol Parasol (J. Mayer H., 2004–2011): close to 30 m high, six parasols over about 150 m, the walkway across their tops; orientation in three directions for every version: the Giralda and cathedral to the south; west toward the river, Triana's rooftops and the Aljarafe beyond; north toward the Macarena district, about a kilometre away (direction only, no landmark claimed). ONSITE: O7 (cathedral body in clear view), O8 (Giralda-on-your-left cue; Triana's rooftops), O9 (north view; skyline boards; "Giralda at your back" cue).
tracks.listen: How high you are, the three directions to fix, and the whole building stacked up beneath you.

tracks.title: Walkway — Love it or hate it
tracks.where: On the walkway after you come back down from the Mirador, heading toward the way down; walking, or stopped at the rail out of the way of others.
tracks.what: The controversy over Metropol Parasol: protests at the opening on 27 March 2011, the critics' verdict "como a un Cristo dos pistolas", Rowan Moore's review as relayed by Dezeen (paper not named), Mayor Alfredo Sánchez Monteseirín's "moderna catedral urbana"; the four-year delay, overlapping Spain's financial crisis, and the cost the city reported to Spain's Ombudsman, without the museum figure; Red Dot "Best of the Best" 2012, Mies van der Rohe Award finalist 2013, over a million visitors in the first year by one count. V5 013 kept as fixed, plus one sentence on the crisis.
tracks.listen: Why Seville argued about the Setas for years, what it cost, and what it won.

tracks.title: Walkway · Extra · Aurora, the Setas after dark
tracks.where: Anywhere on the walkway or at the Mirador, by day or after dark; stop at the rail out of the way of others.
tracks.what: Metropol Parasol Aurora (2021, for the tenth anniversary): an LED light and sound installation built into the timber; by the architects' own office, J. MAYER H. (partners in charge Jürgen Mayer H. and Andre Santer), with concept and software by Skandal Technologien; fourteen light patterns, twelve for commemorative dates; responds to visitor numbers and movement, weather, wind and season, with special programmes for days such as Semana Santa and the Feria; under 30% of the lights on at once. ONSITE: O15 (running on the day; fittings visible by day).
tracks.listen: The light show built into the timber, who made it, and how it reacts to the crowd, the weather and the calendar.

tracks.room: Feeling Sevilla · before you go in
tracks.title: Feeling Sevilla · Extra · The room at 21 metres
tracks.where: Outside the entrance to the Feeling Sevilla room, the Sala Feeling, before you go in; follow the signs for Feeling Sevilla and stand aside from the door.
tracks.what: Sala Feeling, the multisensory room of Feeling Sevilla (Sacyr, 2021): about 21 m above the ground, over 200 m², stands for 96 people, curved LED screen 21 × 3 m, 360º sound, floor projection, air and scent effects; film about 15 minutes. The level inside the parasols in the architects' plan, on a steel-and-concrete platform. Nothing on the film's content. ONSITE: O11 (where the room is and when it comes in the route).
tracks.listen: What the film room is, how it was added in 2021, and why not everything up here is wood.

tracks.title: The way down — From building site to city symbol
tracks.where: On the way down from the walkways to the Plaza Mayor, where the exhibition on the history of the Plaza de la Encarnación lines the route; play it as you walk down.
tracks.what: The official exhibition on the way down, showing the evolution of the Plaza de la Encarnación up to today (contents not yet photographed); building the Setas from June 2005; the opening on Sunday 27 March 2011 by Mayor Alfredo Sánchez Monteseirín, the Antiquarium the same evening; Arup's project director José de la Peña; Sacyr's concession and the 2021 renewal; DATED: 15th anniversary in 2026. ONSITE: O12 (exhibition contents; where the way down comes out), O14.
tracks.listen: How a building site Seville argued over became a city symbol, as you walk down past the exhibition.

tracks.title: Plaza Mayor — Under the timber
tracks.where: On the Plaza Mayor, the big raised square under the parasols, where the way down comes out; stand out of the way, somewhere you can see the timber overhead.
tracks.what: The Plaza Mayor of Metropol Parasol (J. Mayer H., opened 2011): almost 4,000 m², about 5 m above the street, on the roof of the market; the operator says it is the largest shaded pedestrian plaza in Seville and noticeably cooler even on very hot days, designed for large events (sport, music, fairs, performing arts); overhead, the Kerto-Q panels of the parasols in an orthogonal grid about 1.5 m apart, shady yet open to the sky; two of the trunks hold the lifts, inside concrete (the wording VS-SET, JA-SET and PUBSP agree on; the material of the other trunks is not said, audit 018.1, lead decision 5; the trunk is offered only "if you can see one", O14, audit S8); the 2011 indignados (15-M) meetings and camp at the Setas (PUBSP: "chose the site for its camp"; no source puts the camp on the raised square itself, so not "right here", audit 018.2), and the academic reading of them. Moved here from V5 018: the indignados paragraph. ONSITE: O14 (where the way down arrives; whether the trunks are in view from every part of the square).
tracks.listen: How big, how high and how cool this raised square is, what the timber over your head is made of, and how protesters made it theirs in its first weeks.

tracks.title: Plaza Mayor — The market that waited 37 years
tracks.where: On the Plaza Mayor, the big raised square under the parasols; find a quiet spot away from the way down. The market is directly beneath this square, at street level.
tracks.what: The Mercado de la Encarnación: Melchor Cano's market hall of the 1830s, demolished 1973; temporary stalls for three years that lasted 37; the new market at street level under the Plaza Mayor, reopened 19 Dec 2010; fishmongers and greengrocers today. V5 017 kept, trimmed so it does not re-tell 008 (1830s, the 1973 reasons, "fenced, dusty car park"): 008 is always heard first (route audit S11, N9). ONSITE: O14 (where to stand).
tracks.listen: How the market's "temporary" move lasted 37 years, and how it came back under your feet.

tracks.title: Plaza Mayor — The plaza on stilts, and the way out
tracks.where: On the Plaza Mayor, the big raised square on the roof of the market, under the parasols; stand anywhere out of the way, ideally where you can see the parasols overhead.
tracks.what: The Plaza Mayor of Metropol Parasol (J. Mayer H., opened 2011) as public space: the raised square over the Mercado de la Encarnación, open to the sky and used for events, one of the design's four layers; Mayer's "new contemporary urban centre" and "urban, democratic, open cathedral"; finalist, European Prize for Urban Public Space 2012; Aurora after sunset; the way out to the street; the after-visit Extra announced for the full tour; goodbye. The indignados paragraph of V5 018 has moved to 018. ONSITE: O14 (the way to the street; signs), O15 (Aurora season).
tracks.listen: Why the raised square is the heart of the design, how to leave, and a last look back down the whole building.

tracks.title: After your visit · Extra · The fig trees and the Roman columns
tracks.where: Anywhere, after you have left the Setas: on the street, at a café, or on your way to either place. Full tour only, after the last stop.
tracks.what: Two places nearby: the old fig trees (ficus) of the Plaza del Cristo de Burgos, which the city names as an inspiration for the parasols (Mayer himself speaks of "big trees on a neighboring plaza"; the operator calls them centennial), given specialist care by the city (VIVIR); the fig-tree facts are told in full in 009 and only called back here (audit M3); and the two Roman columns of the Alameda de Hércules, of the Trajan–Hadrian period and possibly from a temple (JA-COL's word, audit 021.1), set up there in 1574 on the orders of the Count of Barajas, with statues of Hercules, the city's mythical founder, and Julius Caesar. No bars, prices, hours or walking times. ONSITE: none (position-free); O20 re-check of the ficus works before recording.
tracks.listen: Where to find the trees the parasols are said to echo, and a piece of Roman Seville that has stood above ground for four and a half centuries.
